correctness.rationale: The cited half-period theorem applies: B=sin t>0 on (0,π), A is half-period even and has the required +−+ sign pattern there, B reverses sign after π, and the transformed convexity numerator is ≥3(1+a)>0. Independently, writing b=∫B=1−cos t, u=∫A, return coefficients of orders 3,4,5 are u(T), ∫bA, and ∫b²A+3u(T)²/2 by triangular expansion and integration by parts. This verifies the scale 2√(−a). A positive periodic solution's parameter derivative has a strictly negative periodic Green formula because its multiplier exceeds one. Near a=−1 each surviving positive orbit is cut down to ≤4 over [π/4,3π/4]; x^(−2) then satisfies w'≥−w/4−2δ, forcing any periodic initial condition ≤8 for δ≤0.001. The same inequality ensures a bounded flow on [0,T] from 0≤r≤8 for δ≤0.0001. At δ=0 the integrated reciprocal equation precludes a periodic solution, and uniform negative small-r displacement plus compactness on the remaining interval transfer nonexistence to δ>0 small. At any putative interior right endpoint, positive initial conditions stay away from zero by the small-r sign and entire profiles are bounded from above by monotonicity; continuous dependence and hyperbolicity extend the component, a contradiction. Early-time x'≥κx³ bounds left-endpoint initial values uniformly, but existence to T at the limit would extend the forbidden branch. A finite terminal positive solution must tend to +∞ since even a bounded subsequence would give a common positive lifespan by local ODE continuation. Bounded maxima on a subsequence would instead give a periodic limit. The supplied numerical checks were read as samples, not used as evidence of a certified threshold.
